title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

errors: No mathematical error. The example is consistent with the definitions: e has order 0 and is in 𝔓; a has order 1 and is in 𝔓; d has order 1 and is not in 𝔓; c has order 2 and is in 𝔓; b has order 2 and is not in 𝔓.
Minor slip: the formula 𝔓_0 = 𝔓 ∩ M_0 contains a garbled overwritten '𝔓 ∩ L'. M_0 = L, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Classification of vertices of a finite union of points and open intervals on a line into five types (isolated, proper/improper boundary, proper/improper interior) via the order of incidence and membership
ideas.modern_name: Local types of points in a 1-dimensional constructible/semi-algebraic set or o-minimal 1-cell decomposition; Euler-characteristic bookkeeping for constructible functions on R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s); semi-algebraic geometry
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this combinatorial zoology is unpublished

ideas.what: Terminology: interval S_{a,b} (open 1-cell) vs segment = its closure {S_{a,b}, a, b}; redundant ('morcellement') vs lacunary vertices
ideas.modern_name: Open 1-cell and closed cell (closure); subdivision vertex vs puncture

ideas.what: Crossed-out classification of intervals in a préfigure as closed or semi-open according to how many endpoints are proper vertices
ideas.modern_name: Closed, half-open and open 1-cells relative to a constructible set

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, carefully worked combinatorial bookkeeping of point types in 1-dimensional 'figures'. It is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial tame topology, which is historically interesting as context. The content itself is routine and nothing on the page goes beyond what any 1-dimensional cell-decomposition treatment contains.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans le polyèdre' should read 'Dans la préfigure'.

The struck line '[-Pour une intervalle-]' and the following 'puisque appelles' are more plausibly '[Pour un intervalle (struck)] Je préfère : puisse appeler S_{a,b} = S_{b,a} ou S_{{a,b}} un intervalle (plutôt qu'un segment)'.
'Le segment associé à l'intervalle est S̃_{a,b} = {S_{a,b}, a, b} — i.e. la multiplicité complète associée : S̄_{a,b}' — the 'Le' before 'segment' is itself struck in the image.
'𝔓_0 = 𝔓 ∩ M_0 = 𝔓_0 L' should be '𝔓_0 = 𝔓 ∩ M_0 = 𝔓 ∩ L, 𝔓_1 = 𝔓 ∩ M_1', with 𝔓_0 underbraced as 'ou ens. des sommets propres'.
In the crossed-out final paragraph, the middle of the closed-interval condition reads 'i.e. ∂X ⊂ 𝔓_0' (written above 'X̄ ⊂ 𝔓'). It ends '(semi-ouverts dans ...)'.
Figure: a is drawn as a filled endpoint, b as an empty puncture '( )', c as a filled point '(•)', d as an open end '(', and e as an isolated dot.
